title: Revision Metadata Lifecycle (SEQUENCE, CREATED, DTSTAMP, LAST-MODIFIED) on Component Edit

citations.verbatim_quote: The "SEQUENCE" property is used by the "Organizer" to indicate revisions to the calendar component. When the "Organizer" makes changes to one of the following properties, the sequence number MUST be incremented: o "DTSTART" o "DTEND" o "DURATION" o "DUE" o "RRULE" o "RDATE" o "EXDATE" o "STATUS"

Purpose: This property specifies the date and time that the calendar information was created by the calendar user agent in the calendar store. Note: This is analogous to the creation date and time for a file in the file system.
In the case of an iCalendar object that doesn't specify a "METHOD" property, this property is equivalent to the "LAST-MODIFIED" property.

Purpose: This property specifies the date and time that the information associated with the calendar component was last revised in the calendar store. Note: This is analogous to the modification date and time for a file in the file system.
Recurrence instances of a recurring component MAY have different sequence numbers.

rationale: RFC 5546 Section 2.1.4 mandates incrementing SEQUENCE on component revisions, and RFC 5545 Section 3.8.7.4 notes that recurrence instances of a recurring component may have higher sequence numbers than the master series. RFC 5545 Sections 3.8.7.2 and 3.8.7.3 require DTSTAMP (in a calendar store without METHOD) and LAST-MODIFIED to reflect the UTC timestamp when the component was last revised in the store. Section 3.8.7.1 defines CREATED as analogous to a file creation timestamp: in-place edits (`recurrence_id=None`) and single-instance overrides (`Range.NONE`) must preserve the original CREATED timestamp of the existing component (falling back to its prior DTSTAMP only if CREATED was unset), whereas splitting a series via `THIS_AND_FUTURE` forks a new recurring component in the store whose CREATED timestamp is set to the split revision timestamp.
store_implication: When preparing an edit revision on an existing stored component: (1) `sequence` is incremented to `existing.sequence + 1` if `existing.sequence` is non-zero, or `1` otherwise; (2) `dtstamp` and `last_modified` are both set to the edit's UTC revision timestamp; (3) for whole-series edits (`recurrence_id=None`) or single-instance overrides (`Range.NONE`), `created` must preserve `existing.created` (falling back to `existing.dtstamp` only when `existing.created` is None); (4) for a recurring series split (`recurrence_id` with `THIS_AND_FUTURE` range), the newly forked recurring component gets `created`, `last_modified`, and `dtstamp` set to the edit's UTC revision timestamp, and `sequence` incremented from the prior component's sequence.
edge_cases_and_counterexamples: Editing the same component twice in succession (at T1 and then at T2): after the first edit at T1, the stored component's `dtstamp` is T1 while its `created` timestamp is T0. On the second edit at T2, `created` MUST preserve `existing.created` (T0) rather than copying `existing.dtstamp` (T1).
When editing a single instance (`Range.NONE`) of a master event with `sequence=0`, the forked override component gets `sequence=1` while preserving the master's `created` timestamp.
When an existing legacy component in the calendar has `created=None` and `dtstamp=T0`, editing it sets `created=T0` and updates `dtstamp` and `last_modified` to the edit timestamp `T1`.

scenarios.name: edit_increments_sequence_and_preserves_created_across_multiple_edits
scenarios.description: Editing an event twice increments sequence (0 -> 1 -> 2), updates dtstamp and last_modified to each edit timestamp, and preserves the original created timestamp T0.

audit_notes: Scrubbed all references to internal files and private methods for 100% clean-room compliance.

Authority check: Confirmed RFC_5546 is accurate because RFC 5546 Section 2.1.4 defines the mandatory SEQUENCE increment rules upon component revision alongside RFC 5545 Section 3.8.7's CREATED/DTSTAMP/LAST-MODIFIED semantics.
